summary:
Illes Balears stands under Spain's Ley 4/2023 of 28 February 2023, published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado, which establishes real and effective equality for trans persons and guarantees LGTBI rights and applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities. No source in the inventory records a Balearic deviation from that framework.

Article 43 allows any person aged 16 or over to request rectification of the gender mention on their own registry entry directly before the Civil Registry, an administrative route grounded in the free development of personality under article 10.1 of the Constitution. It replaces the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment. Recognition is possible from age 12 under conditions, a provision Human Rights Watch reported as contentious when the Congress passed the law.

Access to sex-separated facilities rests on legal gender self-determination rather than on biological sex, so the gender marker recorded in the civil registry is the operative basis for facility rules and determines which facilities a visitor may use.

The law defines and sanctions discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics, and declares discriminatory contract clauses null and void. Human Rights Watch records that it combats LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing and strengthens protections for unmarried same-sex couples.

Transphobic motivation operates as an aggravating circumstance in sentencing under Article 22.4 of the Criminal Code, and the hate-speech provision at Article 510 carries one to four years' imprisonment plus a fine of six to twelve months; both derive from Organic Law 6/2022 rather than from Ley 4/2023. Gender expression appears in no article of the Criminal Code, so a gender-expression-based hate crime has no free-standing offence. Ley 4/2023 did reform the offences against sexual freedom at Articles 132, 173, 178 to 181 and 189 bis.

Courts are applying the aggravation in practice. A Tribunal de Instancia in Vigo used the transfobia aggravation for the first time, in a misdemeanour case over WhatsApp messages threatening a trans woman, and fined the author EUR 300. In Valencia, a juvenile gang that harassed, insulted, beat and filmed a trans person in a park to mock them produced a six-month prison sentence for the only adult defendant, while two minors were judged separately.

Same-sex marriage and full adoption rights have applied in Spain since 2005.
tangentialFactors:
With administrative self-declaration, Spain stands alongside Argentina, Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay, and is recognised in comparative rankings as among the most LGBT-friendly countries.

The provision allowing recognition from age 12 proved contentious during the law's passage, and it sits alongside the regulation of consent for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16.

The aggravating circumstance and the hate-speech offence both rest on Organic Law 6/2022, so the sentencing tools a trans person can invoke do not come from the trans statute itself.
localsOnly:
Residents may rectify the registry gender mention directly before the Civil Registry without prior surgical reassignment, and the law obliges discrimination data collection broken down by the causes it covers.

Discriminatory contract clauses are declared null and void, and the statute mandates measures adapted to rural circumstances across the Balearic territory.

Human Rights Watch records strengthened protections for unmarried same-sex couples and combatting of LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing, all of which bear on resident access to services.

The law regulates consent for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16, and recognition of gender from age 12 is possible under conditions.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory records a Balearic instance of the transfobia aggravation being applied; the two documented cases come from Vigo and Valencia.

Whether the Illes Balears Civil Registry or the regional courts apply Ley 4/2023 differently from other autonomous communities is unresolved here: no regional deviation is documented in either direction.

Facility access is stated at the level of the national rule. How specific Balearic venues verify a registry marker in practice is not sourced.

Enforcement of the Article 510 hate-speech provision and of the discrimination sanctions is not broken down by region in the inventory.
